record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Characterize the secure polygons. In particular, give a criterion deciding when a rational polygon is secure, where a pair of points is secure if finitely many blocking points intersect every billiard orbit joining the pair.

evidence.quote: Задача 15. Охарактеризовать безопасные многоугольники. В частности, установить критерий безопасности для рациональных многоугольников.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider billiard dynamics in a planar polygon $P$. A billiard trajectory is the path of a point particle moving in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary, with trajectories hitting vertices left undefined. For two points $x,y \in P$, a blocking set for the pair $(x,y)$ is a finite set $B \subset P \setminus \{x,y\}$ such that every billiard trajectory from $x$ to $y$ passes through some point of $B$. The pair $(x,y)$ is called secure if such a finite blocking set exists. The polygon $P$ is called secure if every pair of points $(x,y)$ in $P$ is secure.

A polygon is called rational if all of its interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$.

(a) Give an intrinsic characterization of all secure polygons.

(b) In particular, find a criterion that decides, in terms of the geometry of $P$, when a rational polygon $P$ is secure.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial results are known. Monteil and Hubert–Schmoll–Troubetzkoy have shown that among regular polygons only the square, equilateral triangle, and regular hexagon have the finite blocking property; a Veech (lattice) surface is secure iff it is "arithmetic" (a torus cover). Local obstructions to finite blocking on translation surfaces have been established, yielding classifications for L-shaped surfaces. However, a general intrinsic characterization of secure polygons, and a complete criterion for arbitrary rational polygons, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Blocking of billiard orbits and security for polygons and flat surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: A lattice polygon is secure if and only if it is arithmetic; partial results toward characterizing secure polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterization established for lattice (Veech) polygons.

status_evidence.title: On the finite blocking property
status_evidence.snippet: Among regular polygons, only the square, equilateral triangle, and regular hexagon have the finite blocking property.
status_evidence.claim: Restricted classification; the general criterion for rational polygons remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Illumination in Rational Billiards (arXiv:1905.09358)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses related blocking/illumination problems for rational billiards with open cases remaining.
status_evidence.claim: The full security criterion for rational polygons is still open.
